chunks.text:
Crime Case Study: The Axe Wielding Parolee
In 2007, two police officers from a county sheriff's office in Texas stopped a vehicle they thought was being driven by a suspect wanted for a parole violation. The suspect vehicle pulled over into the busy parking lot of a gas station without incident.
When the officers verified that the driver, John Ledbetter, 38, was wanted for a parole violation, they called for backup because he had a reputation for violence. When two more county sheriff officers arrived, the suspect was asked to get out of his vehicle. To the dismay of the officers, John Ledbetter came out of his vehicle wielding a large, long-handled axe.
After Ledbetter repeatedly refused to put down his weapon, officers sprayed him with pepper spray. Surprisingly, this did stop him. Instead, he got back into his vehicle and attempted to drive away. Before he could do so, one of the officers leaned into the vehicle and began trying to remove the axe from Ledbetter's hand by hitting him several times with a baton. Amazingly, this still did not stop Ledbetter, but the officer was able to remove the keys from the ignition. Ledbetter then got out of the vehicle again with the axe. Fearing for the safety of several people in the parking lot, police officers ordered the bystanders to go into the gas station where the attendant locked the doors. By this time, two more officers from the local county sheriff's department arrived resulting in six officers being at the scene. Despite their overwhelming number, officers were still unable to convince Ledbetter to drop the axe and surrender. With their firearms drawn, officers were able to surround Ledbetter near the back of the gas station.
When, two local city police officers armed with CEDs arrived at the scene. Although these two officers attempted to convince Ledbetter to drop the axe and surrender, he continued to refuse. As a result, one of the city police officers used his CED upon Ledbetter. After one shot, he was in complete compliance. The officers involved and their superiors all agreed that the use of the CED likely prevented the loss of life in this potentially violent standoff.
